title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms
summary: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision published final reforms to the Basel III framework in December 2017, addressing excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs) through enhanced standardised approaches, constrained use of internal models, and a revised leverage ratio with capital floor. Implementation dates span from January 2022 through January 2027, with the output floor ramping from 50% to 72.5%.
key_points: Key objective is reducing excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs) across banks, restoring credibility in reported capital ratios

Three main changes: (i) enhanced standardised approaches for credit and operational risk, (ii) constrained use of internally-modelled approaches, (iii) finalized leverage ratio with revised capital floor
Standardised approach for credit risk, CVA framework, and operational risk framework all have 1 January 2022 implementation dates
The 1.06 scaling factor applied to IRB RWA amounts will be removed upon implementation
BIS conducted quantitative impact study and calibration to avoid significantly increasing overall capital requirements
Jurisdictions may implement more conservative requirements or accelerated transitional arrangements as Basel constitutes minimum standards only
why_it_matters: These reforms fundamentally reshape how banks calculate capital requirements, affecting risk-weighted assets across the global banking system. The output floor constrains banks' ability to reduce capital requirements through internal models, making capital ratios more comparable and transparent. This directly affects how banks structure their balance sheets, price credit risk, and allocate capital across business lines. The phased implementation allows banks to adjust gradually.
macro_context: As a post-crisis regulatory reform, these changes were designed to strengthen banking system resilience and support sustainable economic growth over the medium term. The Committee explicitly calibrated to avoid significantly increasing overall capital requirements, balancing prudential goals with avoiding adverse macro-economic impact.
market_structure_context: The reforms directly address market structure by enhancing the robustness of standardised approaches for credit and operational risk, improving comparability of banks' capital ratios. The output floor mechanism constrains internal model arbitrage, making the regulatory framework more uniform across institutions.
important_numbers: 1 January 2022 implementation for standardised credit risk, CVA, and operational risk frameworks
